  AMENDED AGENDA - ITEM NO. 7B

In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493, 2498,
2499, 2503 and 2505 due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives
as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being broadcast via teleconference. Members of
the public may participate in-person in the Council Chambers, or virtually in the meeting in the following ways:

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
897 9511 9566 Passcode: 996653. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call in option from
a phone line.)

- Public correspondence may be emailed to the carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00
p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the Planning Commission for their consideration and
included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an
“eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp
page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen
by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 897 9511 9566 Passcode: 996653.

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, MAY 9, 2022

An adjourned meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order by CHAIR SCHACHTER at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes
Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274, and via teleconference pursuant to Assembly Bill 361.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Carman, Low, Olson, Edler

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development & Public Works
  Don Davis, City Attorney
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Dean Flores, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, MARCH 7, 2022

COMMISSIONER CARMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 7, 2022.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

VICE CHAIR YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE ITEM NO. 6A

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PA-220097; ADDRESS: 21 CLUB VIEW LANE, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274;
  APPLICANT: MATT SCHNEIDER; DESCRIPTION: A request for a Neighborhood
  Compatibility Determination (NC-220098) for a new, two-story 4,965.5 sq. ft. single-family
  floor deck, 650.68 sq. ft. covered patio, and 64 sq. ft. in-ground jacuzzi.

Dean Flores, Associate Planner provided a presentation on Planning Application No. 220097,
summarizing the staff report. The second-story addition will be limited to the west side of the
property with a maximum height of 24’-6”, which is less than the maximum allowable height of
27’.

Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
Planning Application PA-220097, approving a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-
220098) for a new two-story home featuring an attached three-car garage, a second-story deck,

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MAY 9, 2022
  1
 covered patio, and in-ground spa, subject to the conditions of approval in the staff report.

VICE CHAIR YOO asked if correspondence was received from neighbors from 19 to 24 Club
View Lane. Associate Planner stated that correspondence was received from 20 Club View Lane
in regards to a tree that is blocking their view; a copy was included as an attachment to the staff
report.

Matt Schneider, Architect, stated that he has not had any discussion with his client regarding the
trees. Director Wahba stated that the trees in question are City trees, located in the public right-
of-way, and removal will need to go through the City’s Community Service Department.

COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that the request to remove any trees should go through the
process and evaluate that the character of the street is not lost by removal of the tree(s).

Mr. Schneider stated that per the site survey, there is a 5’ wide easement for public utilities, and
the trees are within the easement. Mr. Schneider requested clarification since it seems that the
trees are on his clients’ property. Director Wahba stated that the public right-of-way on Club View
Lane typically extends 8’ to 10’ from the curb. Planning Manager Naughton stated that, if the
survey is accurate, the trees are on private property. Staff agreed to verify whether the trees are
on private property or in the public right-of-way.

Mr. Schneider stated that in regards to the trees, he does not believe his client will have any
issues with the removal of the tree(s). In regards to the survey, he believes the survey is accurate.

Mr. Schneider added that his client desired a more contemporary design. He further added that
he designed the second story to one side considering to not block views, privacy, and keep
traditional roof lines to blend into the neighborhood.

Planning Manager Naughton clarified that the tract map (attachment H of the staff report) shows
that there is a 5’ easement to the City of Rolling Hills Estates for planting and public utilities
purposes.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked about noting the location of trash cans so that the applicant is
aware that they cannot be in a location that can be viewed from the street. Mr. Schneider stated
that there is an area on the east side of the property and it is outside of the 10’ setback.
Planning Manager Naughton stated that in the residential districts, trash enclosures are not
required; however, they need to be obscured from public views. Staff can require that this be
noted on the plans prior to zone clearance and obtaining building permits.

COMMISSIONER LOW asked when the neighboring house was built. Director Wahba stated that
this property was never developed; it was subdivided in the 1960’s.

COMMISSIONER EDLER stated that he likes the overall design and that the architect recognized
the view options. He finds that the design is tasteful and a contemporary style that fits in with the
neighboring houses.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked if the concern from the neighbor in regards to height needs
to be addressed since they are under the maximum height limit. Director Wahba stated that there
are not issues with height.

COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220097 AND THAT THE APPLICANT
  WORK WITH STAFF TO ADDRESS THE ISSUE WITH THE TREES.

AYES: Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Carman, Low, Olson, Edler
NOES:
ABSENT:
ABSTAIN:

Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission approved Planning Application
No. 220097, approving a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-220098) for a new two-
story residence. There is a 20-day appeal period by where any member of the public or the City
Council, by its own motion, may appeal this project to the City Council.

B.  PA-220102; ADDRESS: 44 ENCANTO DRIVE, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274;
  APPLICANT: JOHN JUGE; DESCRIPTION: A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility
  Determination (NC-220103) for a 714 sq. ft. single-story addition and a 1,354 sq. ft.
  second-story addition to an existing single-story single-family residence.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MAY 9, 2022
  2
 Dean Flores, Associate Planner provided a presentation on Planning Application No. 220102,
summarizing the staff report. The second story is setback approximately 20’ on the south side
and 10’ on the north side, in order to provide articulation and provide privacy of the adjacent
neighbors. Correspondence was received from the owners of 13 Dorado Place, which is located
at the rear of the property; they expressed concerns with the view of the home due to missing
landscaping in the public right-of-way. The applicant agreed to install landscaping of similar
material and size to cover the missing portion of landscaping.

An additional correspondence was received in regards to the second-story bathroom windows,
maintenance of trees in the rear yard to maintain privacy, and possible replacement of a tree that
died and was cut down in the front yard.

Staff recommends adding two additional conditions of approval to address the missing
landscaping and require that the applicant provide obscuring material on the second-story north-
facing bathroom windows and that this be noted on the plans.

Associate Planner Flores recommends that the issue with the trees be resolved between the
applicant and the neighbor unless the Planning Commission decides otherwise.

Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
PA-220102 for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-220103) for a 714 sq. ft. single-
story addition and a 1,354 sq. ft. second-story addition to an existing single-story single-family
residence subject to the revised conditions of approval.

VICE CHAIR YOO asked about the correspondence received from Jane Nicklas with concerns
regarding the solar panels. Associate Planner Flores stated that the City does not have discretion
on installation of solar panels. In speaking with Mrs. Nicklas, she was satisfied with the additional
condition to address the missing landscaping in order to address the view to the home and the
concern with the solar panels did not come up again.

John Juge, Applicant, stated that the solar panels will be located on the south side roof; with the
installation of the missing landscaping the home will not be visible to the neighbor. Mr. Juge stated
that the sill of the window is 6’ 6” above finished floor in the bathroom, and he has no issue with
making it obscure. Mr. Juge stated that he has spoken with Mr. Choo (neighbor) to consider their
concerns.

David Choo, 46 Encanto Drive, stated that this is a big improvement from the original proposal.
He stated that he understands that compromises need to be made and stated that he is concerned
with a two-story house among single-story houses, but this is a decision of the Planning
Commission. His concern is with privacy. Mr. Choo stated that the trees in the rear provide privacy
and would like those trees to remain and be maintained. Mr. Choo also requested that the tree
that was removed in the front yard be replaced with another tree and maintained since this will
provide privacy from the second story as well.

COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that he is personal friends of the applicant and they have not
discussed this project nor is there any bias in making a decision on this project.

CHAIR SCHACHTER asked how many homes in the neighborhood are two stories. Director
Wahba stated that about 30% of homes in the Montecillo neighborhood are two stories.

COMMISSIONER EDLER stated that he likes the project and appreciates that the applicant is
willing to work with the neighbor on the missing portion of landscaping.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that the only issue is with privacy, but it seems that the
applicant and neighbor are addressing their concerns. He stated that he is in support of this
project.

COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220102 AS PRESENTED.

AYES: Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Carman, Low, Olson, Edler
NOES:
ABSENT:
ABSTAIN:

Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission approved Planning Application
No. 220102, approving a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-220103) for first and
second story additions. There is a 20-day appeal period by where any member of the public or

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING

  3
 the City Council, by its own motion, may appeal this project to the City Council.

C.  PA-220155; ADDRESS: 7 CLUB VIEW LANE, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274;
  APPLICANT: JULIET GERACI; DESCRIPTION: A request for a Neighborhood
  Compatibility Determination (NC-220156) for a 211 sq. ft. single-story addition, and 200
  sq. ft. second-story addition (411 sq. ft. total addition) to an existing two-story single-family
  residence. The proposal also includes a re-roof and site work in the front yard to reduce
  the front yard coverage from 68% to 30%.

Dean Flores, Associate Planner provided a presentation on Planning Application No. 220155,
summarizing the staff report. This project includes a 211 sq. ft. addition towards the rear of the
home and a 200 sq. ft. second-story addition towards the front of the home. The style of the home
will go from Spanish style to a Contemporary Farmhouse style.

Initially, the proposal included removing the circular driveway and create two separate driveways.
The applicant removed the second driveway and provided a revised site plan. Per the City’s
municipal code, driveways must lead to a designated parking area (garage).

Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends adding a condition of approval regarding
the removal of the secondary driveway. Staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
Planning Application No. PA-220155, approving a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination
(NC-220156) for a 211 sq. ft. single-story addition at the rear of the home, and a 200 sq. ft. second-
story addition, updated exterior façade and interior remodel, subject to the revised conditions of
approval.

Juliet Geraci, Architect, stated that her client is the son of the original owner of the home when it
was built in 1971. He and his family would like to make this their “forever home”. There is also an
Accessory Dwelling Unit being built (on a separate permit) for his mother. They desired a clean
and modern style for their home.

VICE CHAIR YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 220155 AS PRESENTED.

AYES: Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Carman, Low, Olson, Edler
NOES:
ABSENT:
ABSTAIN:

Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission approved Planning Application
No. 220155, approving a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-220156) for first and
second story additions. There is a 20-day appeal period by where any member of the public or
the City Council, by its own motion, may appeal this project to the City Council.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PA-220115; LOCATION: CITYWIDE; APPLICANT: CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES;
  A Public Hearing to adopt a Resolution recommending City Council approval of an
  Ordinance amending and restating Rolling Hills Estates Municipal Code Chapter 17.60
  (Signs). The proposed amendments include: (1) expending the purposes of the chapter;
  (2) revising definitions and adding new terms; (3) establishing policies for the interpretation
  and implementation of the chapter; (4) providing additional opportunities for the display
  temporary noncommercial signs; (5) making minor changes to permitted commercial
  signs; (6) expanding the list of prohibited sign structures or types; (7) enhancing the design
  criteria; and (8) revising the appeal and enforcement procedures.

Don Davis, City Attorney, provided a presentation with the proposed key changes to RHEMC
Chapter 17.60 - Sign Code. Most changes are to policy matters, providing clarification, and legal
updates.

COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked about the allowable size of a non-commercial versus
commercial sign in regards to the substitution clause. City Attorney Davis stated that they would
be allowed the same sign area and added that rarely has commercial signage been used for non-
commercial speech.

VICE CHAIR YOO inquired about the two signs that are allowable for non-commercial signs and
how that number was determined. City Attorney Davis stated that we need to provide “reasonable
opportunities”, and it was determined that two signs is reasonable.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MAY 9, 2022
  4
 COMMISSIONER CARMAN requested clarification on the size of signs allowed in residential
zones. City Attorney Davis stated that the sign may not exceed 8 sq. ft.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about the static window signs for the commercial-general
zone. City Attorney Davis stated that these could be interchangeable static signs and need to be
high-quality.

City Attorney Davis stated that the recommendation is that the Planning Commission approve
Resolution No. PA-220115, recommending to the City Council adoption of the presented text
amendments.

VICE CHAIR YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

COMMISSIONER CARMAN expressed her concern with the amount of non-commercial signs
and the length of time that they can be displayed in residential zones. City Attorney Davis stated
that if these actions are not taken and the code can be challenged and instead of allowing two
small signs, they could have (for example) fifty signs because the City has no regulations in place.

VICE CHAIR YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

VICE CHAIR YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER EDLER to,

  ADOPT RESOULUTION NO. PA-220115 RECOMMENDING THAT THE CITY COUNCIL
  APPROVE OF AN  ORDINANCE AMENDING AND RESTATING ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 17.60.

AYES: Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Carman, Low, Olson, Edler
NOES:
ABSENT:
ABSTAIN:

Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has adopted Resolution No.
PA-220115. Staff will be drafting an ordinance that will be presented for review by the City Council
at its meeting on May 24th.

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER EDLER asked about the trees along the Casaba berm. Director Wahba stated
that staff is working on this.

10.  MANAGER ITEMS

Planning Manager Naughton stated that she hopes that the Planning Commissioners that were
able to go on the tours of The Residences at RHCC enjoyed their time.

Planning Manager Naughton stated that the next Planning Commission of June 6th will be a hybrid
meeting.
